scope: Proposition 5.9 (Closed composition in the final metrics) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 63-64. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the old cap metrics with generic periods and take sufficiently long finite isolation collars for their separate extra exceptional 63 summands. For any fixed finite stack, the sphere tests and sufficiently small ordinary data can be chosen so that, for all sufficiently long finite external negative Y -necks, the oriented closed count Ω, summed over the determinant bits, equals the ordinary composition of its cap states, single intervals, and macro maps, up to one overall sign. The same conclusion holds after sufficiently small further generic changes preserving the genuine-face prescriptions. These data can also satisfy Theorem 7.1.
